question.worked_solution:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{3}+4{n}^{2}-9n-36 & = \\ ({n}^{3}+4{n}^{2})-(9n+36) & = \\ {n}^{2}(n+4)-9(n+4) & = \\ (n+4)\cdot {n}^{2}-(n+4)\cdot 9 & = \\ (n+4)({n}^{2}-9) & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(n+4)({n}^{2}-9)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(n+4)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n+4 & =0 \\ n & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $({n}^{2}-9)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}-9 & =0 \\ {n}^{2} & =9 \\ n & =\pm 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $n=-4,\,\pm 3.$
